newsitem.title: UK: Clive Securities, Investec to merge desks.
newsitem.headline: Clive Securities, Investec to merge desks.

text.p: London-based discount house Clive Securities Group is to merge its securities activities with the private banking arm of its parent company, South Africa's Investec Bank Ltd, Clive chairman Michael Walker said.
"We're going to put the two entities together and put all the capital together in one vehicle which will put us in a stronger position," Walker told Reuters in an interview.
The move follows money market reforms by the Bank of England, due to come into effect on Monday, which strip Britain's discount houses of their exclusive rights to trade eligible bills with the Bank.
Under the new rules, the range of counterparties able to participate in the central bank's money market dealings will be widened, and gilt repos will become part of daily money market operations.
Walker said Clive was well placed for the changes and had broadened its financial base to prepare for them.
He said just 10 to 15 percent of the company's business was directly related to the discount house side, the remainder including repo trading, proprietary trading and bond and equity lending.
Walker estimated around 20 institutions would initially apply to be counterparties to the Bank under the new rules. "This may build to 30 to 35," he added.
